The Federal Government has launched a maternal and child health insurance initiative in Imo State, targeting 20,000 enrolments, with priority given to vulnerable women, children and eligible members of their households. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Ali Pate, disclosed this on Thursday during the launch of the initiative, saying the programme was designed to improve access to healthcare for pregnant women and children while reducing the financial burden on their families. Pate said the government’s vision for maternal healthcare was to ensure that every woman could access medical attention promptly, receive the care she needed and safely deliver her child. He recalled that at the 2024 Joint Annual Review, he announced that vulnerable women requiring caesarean sections would receive the procedure free of charge. He said the commitment was based on the principle that a family’s financial situation should not determine whether a woman received life-saving care. According to him, the National Health Insurance Authority had since implemented the Financial Access to Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care initiative, also known as the CEmONC Programme. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Today, CEmONC operates in more than 270 hospitals across every state in Nigeria. I thank the state governments, hospital teams and health workers whose efforts have helped make this support available. But our vision must reach beyond emergency response,” he said. He added that the government was working to ensure women accessed healthcare earlier and throughout pregnancy and childbirth. “We must help women connect with the health system earlier before an emergency, and throughout pregnancy and childbirth. That is also the purpose of the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and the Health Sector Strategic Blueprint 2023–2027,” Pate said. The minister explained that the blueprint was designed to save lives, reduce physical and financial hardship and improve healthcare delivery through effective governance, an efficient and equitable health system, stronger health value chains and improved health security. He said the Federal Government had disbursed ₦249.6bn to the Basic Health Care Provision Fund nationwide over the past three years. He said the resources were expected to strengthen healthcare delivery, improve financial protection and expand access for vulnerable Nigerians. The minister also highlighted the Maternal and Neonatal Mortality Reduction Innovation Initiative, known as MAMII, which brings federal and state agencies together to address barriers to maternal and newborn healthcare. He said the programme included connecting women to healthcare facilities, improving facilities, strengthening referrals and emergency transportation, and expanding access to essential services. According to Pate, Imo State had activated the initiative, including its launch at the Umuohiagu Health Centre in Ngor Okpala Local Government Area and the establishment of a state task force. On other federal-state health partnerships, he recalled that the Federal Government and Imo State signed a memorandum of understanding in June to upgrade the General Hospital, Okigwe, into a Federal Medical Centre. He said the agreement followed the approval to convert the Federal Medical Centre, Owerri, into a university teaching hospital, adding that the state government provided the Okigwe hospital as the take-off site while the Federal Government committed to supporting its development. Pate said the partnership was aimed at expanding access to quality healthcare and bringing specialist services closer to residents. Meanwhile, Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, commended the initiative and praised President Bola Tinubu for what he described as the Federal Government’s contributions to the development of the South-East since the end of the Nigerian Civil War. Uzodimma urged participants at the event to support Tinubu’s re-election, saying his administration had continued efforts to develop the region since assuming office in 2023. Chigozie Uzosike
